name: Greg Lopez

summary.text: Taralyn Romero, Lopez's running mate for lieutenant governor, has more than 25 years of experience in the medical industry, according to Lopez's campaign.

Greg Lopez is a former U.S. representative who served a special-election term for Colorado's 4th Congressional District from July 2024 to January 2025, and a former mayor of Parker; he is running as an unaffiliated candidate after two previous runs for governor as a Republican.
He is a U.S. Air Force veteran and former Colorado director of the U.S. Small Business Administration who lives in Elizabeth, Colorado.

experience.text: U.S. Representative, Colorado's 4th Congressional District, July 8, 2024 - January 3, 2025 (special election to complete Ken Buck's term).
Mayor and town administrator of Parker, Colorado, elected at age 27, 1992-1996.
Colorado director of the U.S. Small Business Administration for six years; says his office issued more than $600 million in loans to Colorado small businesses in 2013 alone.
President/CEO of the Denver Hispanic Chamber of Commerce and of the Rocky Mountain Minority Supplier Development Council.

record.title: H.R. 82, Social Security Fairness Act of 2023, final passage
record.detail: Voted Nay; the bill passed 327-75 and was signed into law.

record.title: H.R. 9495, Stop Terror-Financing and Tax Penalties on American Hostages Act, final passage
record.detail: Voted Yea; the bill passed the House 219-184.

record.title: H.R. 9747, Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2025
record.detail: Voted Nay on the government funding bill, which passed 341-82 and was signed into law.

positions.quote: As Governor, I will defend TABOR protections, oppose efforts to weaken taxpayer safeguards, and fight to ensure refunds are returned fairly to the people.
I firmly believe that Colorado taxpayers deserve transparency, accountability, and protection from unchecked government growth.
positions.note: Inferred opposition to Amendment 87 from his general TABOR-defense and anti-tax-growth stance; he does not name the measure directly.

positions.quote: I strongly support the Taxpayer's Bill of Rights because it empowers citizens, limits excessive taxation, and ensures taxpayers have a direct voice in major fiscal decisions.
positions.note: Inferred support for Proposition 136's rate cap from his strong general TABOR support; the measure is not named directly.

positions.quote: I strongly believe every human life has value and deserves dignity, compassion, and respect. I will continue to support policies that protect life while also supporting mothers, families, adoption services, healthcare access, and community-based support systems that help women and children thrive.
positions.note: This is his most recent (2025/2026 campaign) statement and is a softer formulation than a 2022 interview in which, as a Republican candidate for governor, he said of signing a legislative abortion ban, 'Odds are I would sign it' (news.yahoo.com, 2022-05-04). A reviewer may want to double-check whether his current position has in fact moderated or whether this is just different phrasing.

positions.quote: For the last eight years, Colorado Legislature has been passing gun laws that are infringing on the constitutional rights of citizens and that needs to stop.
Colorado should fully cooperate with federal immigration enforcement efforts involving violent criminals, drug traffickers, gang members, and individuals who pose a threat to public safety.

As Governor, I will work to restore local control whenever possible by reducing unnecessary state mandates and empowering counties, municipalities, and school districts to make decisions that best serve their communities.
positions.note: Consistent with his statement in the Aug. 27, 2026 debate with Weiser that he 'would never take local control away from a jurisdiction' (montrosepress.com).

positions.quote: I will lead Colorado in pursuing an "all-of-the-above" energy strategy that supports innovation, affordability, reliability, and job creation.
positions.note: Inferred support for continued natural gas access from his all-of-the-above energy stance; Amendment 82 is not named.

positions.quote: Due to the overbearing environmental and clean energy policies of the Polis administration over the last eight years Colorado families have seen a severe increase in their gas and electric bills across the state.
The Game and Fish will focus on wildlife management, hunting, fishing, and habitat protection and State Parks will focus on managing state parks, trails and recreational facilities.
positions.note: Inferred support for Amendment 83 from his broader pro-hunting/fishing platform; the amendment is not named directly.

positions.quote: I encourage all voters to support the efforts of "Protect Kids Colorado" in passing the three legislative initiatives that will appear on the November general election ballot.
positions.note: Protect Kids Colorado is the campaign behind Propositions 133, 134 and 135 (dailycitizen.focusonthefamily.com, coloradopolitics.com); this record covers Proposition 134 (school sports).

positions.note: Covers Proposition 135 (surgery ban for minors), one of the three Protect Kids Colorado measures.

research_notes: Verified via Ballotpedia and Wikipedia that Lopez served a six-month special-election term in the U.S. House (Colorado's 4th District, July 2024-January 2025, completing Ken Buck's term) as the assignment asked; his only three recorded House votes do not map to any of the 25 statements, so they appear only in record, confirmed directly against clerk.house.gov roll-call XML. His greglopez.co/issues page is undated beyond a 2025 copyright footer, so every quote drawn from it uses 2025-01-01 as a placeholder date; a reviewer may want to check whether the page has been updated since he left the Republican Party in January 2026.
